features.name: Galileo Regio
features.description: Galileo Regio is Ganymede's largest named dark terrain province and one of the oldest recognizable surfaces in the Solar System. Its dense impact record preserves crust that survived before later tectonic extension broke much of Ganymede into younger bright grooved terrain.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 4,439 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS/IAU center: 45.00 N, 127.00 W; app longitude: 127.00 W.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Large dark northern region bounded by brighter grooved belts

details.label: Science value
details.value: A reference area for reading the transition from ancient cratered crust to tectonically resurfaced bright terrain.

features.name: Uruk Sulcus
features.description: Uruk Sulcus is a broad band of bright, grooved terrain that crosses older dark crust. Parallel ridges and troughs show where Ganymede's ice shell stretched, fractured, and was resurfaced by cleaner ice or material brought up from below.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 2,200 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS/IAU center: 3.40 N, 160.00 W; app longitude: 160.00 W.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Bright grooved swath near the Galileo-Regio boundary

details.label: Science value
details.value: One of the clearest places to compare Ganymede's extensional tectonics with rift-like deformation on rocky worlds.

features.name: Mashu Sulcus
features.description: Mashu Sulcus is a long northern belt of grooved terrain. It helps show that Ganymede's bright lanes are not isolated scars; they form a global network that replaced or dissected older dark crust over a large fraction of the moon.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 2,960 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS/IAU center: 34.00 N, 210.00 W; app longitude: 150.00 E.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: High northern grooved belt between darker provinces

features.name: Harpagia Sulcus
features.description: Harpagia Sulcus is a southern grooved lane that illustrates the same extensional style seen across Ganymede's bright terrain. Its position away from Galileo Regio helps make the point that tectonic resurfacing was global rather than confined to one famous hemisphere.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 1,400 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS/IAU center: 11.80 S, 313.50 W; app longitude: 46.50 E.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Southern bright-groove system crossing darker background terrain

features.name: Gilgamesh
features.description: Gilgamesh is the named crater at the center of a much broader relaxed impact complex in Ganymede's southern hemisphere. The surrounding subdued rings and softened topography show how warm ice can slowly flow after an impact and blur what began as sharp relief.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 153 km for the named crater

details.label: Broader context
details.value: The surrounding multi-ring Gilgamesh impact complex is commonly described at several hundred kilometres across.

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS/IAU center: 62.84 S, 124.83 W; app longitude: 124.83 W.

details.label: Science value
details.value: A strong example of viscous relaxation in an icy crust.

features.name: Osiris
features.description: Osiris is a bright ray crater used here as a visual anchor for fresher ice exposures on Ganymede. Its pale ejecta rays stand out because impact excavation exposed cleaner ice that has not yet been fully darkened by space weathering.

details.label: Visual control
details.value: User-verified marker target: about 38 S, 166.5 W on the rendered Ganymede texture.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Bright ray pattern in southern mid-latitudes

details.label: Science value
details.value: Fresh ray craters provide a contrast against Ganymede's old dark terrain and help reveal the brightness of excavated ice.

features.name: Tros
features.description: Tros is an ancient crater whose outline is partly softened by the slow flow of ice. It is useful for explaining palimpsests: impact scars that remain readable even after their topography has been muted by viscous relaxation.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 94 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS/IAU center: 11.14 N, 27.26 W; app longitude: 27.26 W.

details.label: Visual control
details.value: User-verified marker target: about 11 N, 27 W on the rendered Ganymede texture.

features.name: Nanshe Catena
features.description: Nanshe Catena is a short chain of aligned craters in Ganymede's low northern latitudes. Catenae like this are useful evidence for clustered impacts, including debris that arrived in a string rather than as a single isolated body.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 104 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS/IAU center: 15.40 N, 352.90 W; app longitude: 7.10 E.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Compact crater chain near the 0/360 longitude boundary

features.name: Enki Catena
features.description: Enki Catena is a prominent crater chain whose linked pits record a fragmented impactor striking Ganymede in sequence. Its mix of crater-chain form and icy ejecta context makes it a strong comparison point with chain impacts elsewhere in the Jovian system.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 160 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS/IAU center: 38.84 N, 13.86 W; app longitude: 13.86 W.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Northern crater chain close to the prime-meridian side of the texture

features.name: Terah Catena
features.description: Terah Catena is a longer chain of impact craters in Ganymede's low northern terrain. It helps show that crater chains are not just isolated curiosities, but part of the impact record preserved across the moon's icy crust.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 283 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS/IAU center: 7.10 N, 277.60 W; app longitude: 82.40 E.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Low northern crater chain on the east-positive side of the app map

features.name: Memphis Facula
features.description: Memphis Facula is a bright circular patch on Ganymede, interpreted as a palimpsest-like impact scar where the original crater relief has largely relaxed away. It gives the feature set a clear example of a bright icy impact remnant rather than a dark region or linear groove belt.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 361 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS/IAU center: 14.10 N, 131.91 W; app longitude: 131.91 W.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Bright rounded patch close to the Galileo Regio / Uruk Sulcus region

features.name: Buto Facula
features.description: Buto Facula is another bright impact-related patch on Ganymede. Paired with Memphis Facula, it helps show how icy-satellite impacts can leave low-relief bright scars that are very different from fresh bowl-shaped craters on rocky planets.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 245 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS/IAU center: 13.30 N, 203.20 W; app longitude: 156.80 E.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Bright circular feature in low northern latitudes

features.name: Busiris Facula
features.description: Busiris Facula is a broad bright palimpsest-like feature near the grooved terrains around Tiamat and related sulci. It gives the tour another example of a relaxed icy impact scar whose brightness remains easier to read than its relief.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 369 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS/IAU center: 16.00 N, 215.30 W; app longitude: 144.70 E.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Broad bright circular patch near the Tiamat and Marius terrain boundary

features.name: Coptos Facula
features.description: Coptos Facula is a large bright spot in the same family of relaxed impact remnants as Busiris and Memphis. Its low-latitude placement helps compare several palimpsest-style features across Ganymede's bright and dark terrain boundaries.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 329 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS/IAU center: 10.00 N, 209.00 W; app longitude: 151.00 E.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Large low-latitude facula near other bright palimpsest targets

features.name: Lakhmu Fossae
features.description: Lakhmu Fossae is an enormous system of long narrow depressions and furrows crossing much of Ganymede's northern terrain. Its scale connects local grooves and troughs to the broader tectonic architecture of the ice shell.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 3,700 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS/IAU center: 50.40 N, 128.00 W; app longitude: 128.00 W.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Large northern fossa system spanning a wide longitude range

features.name: Zu Fossae
features.description: Zu Fossae is a broad northern system of troughs and furrows associated with Ganymede's tectonic and impact-modified crust. Together with Lakhmu Fossae, it helps show that Ganymede's dark terrain preserves large structural patterns as well as craters.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 2,900 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS/IAU center: 38.50 N, 150.50 W; app longitude: 150.50 W.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Large northern fossa system near the Galileo Regio side of the map

features.name: Anshar Sulcus
features.description: Anshar Sulcus is a grooved terrain lane that has been studied as a key example of Ganymede's tectonic resurfacing. Its ridges, troughs, and local cross-cutting structures help explain how bright terrain was built by extension and shear in the icy shell.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 1,372 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS/IAU center: 18.90 N, 198.70 W; app longitude: 161.30 E.

details.label: Science value
details.value: A good target for discussing groove formation and strike-slip deformation on Ganymede.

features.name: Dardanus Sulcus
features.description: Dardanus Sulcus is a southern grooved terrain belt. It extends the sulci set into Ganymede's southern hemisphere and helps compare resurfaced bright lanes with nearby darker cratered provinces.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 1,500 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS/IAU center: 31.50 S, 12.70 W; app longitude: 12.70 W.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Southern bright terrain close to the prime-meridian side of the texture

features.name: Mysia Sulci
features.description: Mysia Sulci is one of Ganymede's largest named sulci systems, stretching across thousands of kilometres. Its scale makes it a useful capstone feature for explaining that Ganymede's grooved terrain is a global resurfacing network rather than a set of local cracks.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 5,066 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS/IAU center: 7.00 S, 7.80 W; app longitude: 7.80 W.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Very broad sulci system near the prime-meridian side of the texture

features.name: Nicholson Regio
features.description: Nicholson Regio is a southern dark-terrain province that preserves ancient, densely cratered crust. It broadens the tour beyond Galileo Regio and helps compare old dark terrain on different hemispheres of Ganymede.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Dark southern terrain near the 0/360 longitude boundary

details.label: Science value
details.value: A useful contrast with adjacent bright grooved terrain, where tectonic resurfacing was more intense.

features.name: Barnard Regio
features.description: Barnard Regio is a major dark terrain province straddling Ganymede's low southern latitudes. Its broad, cratered surface helps frame the scale of Ganymede's older crustal blocks before the moon's bright grooved lanes cut across them.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 3,200 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS/IAU center: 6.80 S, 11.60 W; app longitude: 11.60 W.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Large dark province near the prime-meridian side of the texture

features.name: Marius Regio
features.description: Marius Regio is one of Ganymede's largest named dark terrain regions. It sits beside bright grooved belts, making it a strong teaching target for how younger tectonic terrain fragmented older cratered crust.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 4,940 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS/IAU center: 2.50 N, 187.70 W; app longitude: 172.30 E.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Broad low-latitude dark terrain near the Uruk and Mashu grooved systems

features.name: Melotte Regio
features.description: Melotte Regio is a large named region on Ganymede's trailing-side terrain. Including it gives the fact sheet a wider longitudinal spread and helps students compare several dark provinces rather than treating Galileo Regio as the whole story.

details.label: IAU diameter
details.value: About 4,100 km

details.label: Coordinate source
details.value: USGS/IAU center: 12.00 S, 245.00 W; app longitude: 115.00 E.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Large southern-leaning dark region on the opposite side from Galileo Regio

features.name: North Polar Cap
features.description: Ganymede's north polar region is brightened by water frost and shaped by charged particles moving through Jupiter's magnetosphere. Because Ganymede has its own internally generated magnetic field, its poles are also tied to auroral activity and plasma interactions unlike any other moon.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Bright high-latitude cap; longitude is a representative anchor rather than a named IAU feature center

details.label: Science value
details.value: Connects surface frost, Jupiter's plasma environment, and Ganymede's unique intrinsic magnetic field.

features.name: South Polar Cap
features.description: Ganymede's south polar region mirrors the northern frost story, with bright water-ice deposits concentrated at high latitude. Future close orbital observations by ESA's JUICE mission should sharpen how the polar caps connect to surface composition, magnetic-field geometry, and plasma weathering.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Bright high southern cap; longitude is a representative anchor rather than a named IAU feature center

details.label: Science value
details.value: A natural endpoint for explaining why Ganymede is both an icy world and a magnetized world.
